What eGFR threshold has been used to exclude patients from receiving gadolinium-based contrast?
ground_truth: An eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 is the threshold; patients below it are excluded or receive contrast only when the benefit outweighs the risk.

question: At what dose was gadopiclenol found non-inferior to gadobutrol, and why can it be dosed lower?
ground_truth: Gadopiclenol at 0.05 mmol/kg was non-inferior to gadobutrol at 0.1 mmol/kg in the PICTURE trial; it can be dosed lower because its T1 relaxivity is much higher than other extracellular agents.

question: How does the half-life of the residual excretion phase compare between linear and macrocyclic GBCAs?
ground_truth: About 25 hours for currently approved linear agents versus about 6 hours for a macrocyclic agent, roughly 5-8 times longer.

question: How did gadolinium retention rank across gadodiamide, gadopentetate, gadoterate and gadoteridol in rodent studies, and how does that ordering relate to chelate structure?
ground_truth: Gadodiamide showed the most retention, followed by gadopentetate, with gadoterate and gadoteridol roughly equal and lowest. The two lowest are macrocyclic; the two highest are linear, and macrocyclic agents release free gadolinium more slowly.

question: Are all linear gadolinium-based contrast agents in ACR Group I?
ground_truth: No. The substituted linear agents gadobenate and gadoxetate are Group II, together with the macrocyclic agents, and Group II has been associated with few if any NSF cases.
note: Tests whether the model oversimplifies linear = high risk.
